html:
Wayang is the puppet theatre of Java and Bali, in which a single puppeteer, the dalang, performs all night with leather shadow puppets or wooden figures, backed by a gamelan orchestra. It has been played for over a thousand years.

Its stories come mostly from the Indian epics, the Ramayana and the Mahabharata, retold with Javanese clowns who mock the powerful. The Wali Songo are said to have used it to teach Islam.

Wayang kulit, the shadow form, was named a masterpiece of intangible heritage by UNESCO in 2003. Leaders from Sukarno on drew on its heroes, and puppeteers still comment on politics. See batik, another Javanese art.
